html:
FlexGlue (ETH Zurich and partners, 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: ALIKED keypoints, DINOv3 ConvNeXt features and a transformer that predicts where each keypoint lands in the other photo; keypoint index pairs. MIT; DINOv3 backbone weights under the DINOv3 licence.

Commercial use: yes.

Speed and memory not measured for: aliked-flexglue.

Details
  • Paper: FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation, arXiv, 2026-10-23
  • Original code: https://github.com/cvg/FlexGlue at 99920296d082
  • Code licence: MIT AND BSD-3-Clause (permissive); files: LICENSE, LICENSE-ALIKED, LICENSE-DINOv3
  • Weights licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License AND BSD-3-Clause
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/cvg/FlexGlue/blob/99920296d082c9405ebfd612d674efe288e74881/README.md#license ; https://github.com/Shiaoming/ALIKED/blob/683d7c65197395c0b3f01ebe76e1084a27e73a65/LICENSE
  • Training data: FlexGlue: the README states no training data and the training code is not released (see the paper). The DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone was pretrained on LVD-1689M (Meta, not released); ALIKED was trained on MegaDepth.
  • Licence note: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone weights (extractor.backbone.*): the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers them; read it before commercial use.
  • Options: max_keypoints = 2048 (>= 1), long_side = 1024 (>= 0), size = 512 (>= 32)
  • Kernel libraries: none (not implemented: data-dependent keypoint and match counts)
  • Variants: aliked-flexglue
  • Outputs: keypoints1, keypoints2, pairs, scores
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): aliked-flexglue 3000x4000 (2.0 GiB peak allocated, 2.5 reserved)

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0052 and p99 <= 0.012 (absolute error of the output keypoints1).

Limitations

  • Sparse output: no dense warp. result.matches() gives the matched points for estimate_pose; pairs are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
  • One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
  • No exportable module: the keypoint and match counts are data-dependent (torch.compile runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
  • Upstream's sparse mode only: no RoMa v2 refiner, no dense or sampled matches and no covisibility score.
  • Two resizes per image as upstream: ALIKED sees a long side of long_side (aspect kept), the descriptor a size x size square whatever the aspect ratio.
